summary: PARENT QUERY (priority): YES at length p+1. This is a short corollary of a published classification, not a new result. Xia–Yuan, Discrete Math. 310 (2010) 1127–1133, Thm 3.1 covers the unsplittable minimal zero-sum sequences of length I(C_n)−1 = ⌊n/2⌋+1. Peng–Sun arXiv:1409.1970v1 restates it verbatim; the primary text returned 403. For even n the only such forms are (2g)^{n/2−1}(x₁g)((n+2−x₁)g) and g^t((n/2)g)((1+n/2)g)^{2ℓ}. For n=2p, both contain an even term: 2g, or (p+1)g. Splittable sequences of that length have index 1. Splitting gives length ⌊n/2⌋+2, which has index 1, and the g-norm cannot increase under splitting. Hence every all-odd minimal zero-sum sequence over C_2p (p≥5 prime) of length p+1 has index 1. Via U·(−σ(U)), every odd zero-sum-free U of length p has index <1. Independent cross-check [INFERENCE]: the Savchev–Chen unsplittable forms u^a v^q (v−su) (JNT 177 (2017); 2016 author slides Thm 3), at n=2p and length p+1, force s=1 (u and u+p both occur) or q=1 (u lies in 2C_2p); either way an even term appears. The boundary does not move lower [INFERENCE, hand-checked]: g^{p−4}((p+2)g)^2(pg) is all-odd, minimal, of length p−1, with index 2 for every prime p≥7 (index 1 at p=5). S1-SHARP: no located source states it or an equivalent length-window statement. Its proof Steps 4/6/7 (a common generator for the two-atom shortest long zero-sum T, with both atoms of coefficient sum 2p) are the k=2 case of Zeng–Yuan, Eur. J. Combin. 32 (2011) 1213–1221 (abstract read). FB: no located equivalent. The nearest two-sided structures (Savchev–Chen 2008 n-zero-free; Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang 2015 Cor. 9) need lengths that never occur here. ORDERED D_2p: unchanged. No located primary result, ordered or unordered, implies the restricted criteria; every dihedral E(G) result located is unordered. This was a bounded screen: a search miss is not novelty, and correctness was not checked here.

findings.claim: Xia–Yuan 2010 Thm 3.1: for even n, the unsplittable minimal zero-sum sequences of length ⌊n/2⌋+1 are exactly two families. Each contains 2g or (1+n/2)g, which are even in C_2p.
findings.quote: If n is even, then either S = (2g)^{n/2−1}(x₁g)((n + 2 − x₁)g), where 2 ∤ x₁, … or S = g^t(n/2 g)((1 + n/2)g)^{2ℓ}, where … t + 2ℓ = n/2. Moreover ind(S) ≥ 2.
findings.source: J. Peng, F. Sun, 'On the unsplittable minimal zero-sum sequences over finite cyclic groups of prime order', Thm 1.3(2), citing Xia & Yuan [26, Theorem 3.1], Discrete Math. 310 (2010) 1127–1133, DOI 10.1016/j.disc.2009.11.029
findings.kind: secondary verbatim restatement of a refereed theorem
findings.verified: Read. PDF extraction lost the '≠' in 'x₁ ≠ n+2−x₁' and some exponent layout. The Xia–Yuan text itself was not read.
findings.scope: Unsplittable minimal zero-sum sequences over C_n of length I(C_n)−1; even n (p≥5 gives n=2p≥10)
findings.read_scope: pp.1–9: abstract, §1 Thms 1.2–1.5, §2 lemmas, §3 proofs including Thm 1.5

findings.claim: Splittable minimal zero-sum sequences of length I(G)−1 have index 1, because splitting cannot lower the g-norm.
findings.quote: Let S be a minimal zero-sum sequence of length I(G) − 1 over a finite cyclic group G. If S is splittable, it is easy to check that ind(S) = 1.
findings.source: Peng–Sun §1 p.2. The proof of their Thm 1.5 gives the mechanism: 'Clearly ‖T‖_g ≤ ‖T′‖_g for every g ∈ G \ {0}. Hence ind(T) ≤ ind(T′) = 1.'
findings.kind: secondary statement plus an explicit one-line proof in the same paper

findings.claim: The zbMATH review of Xia–Yuan states the theorem in a garbled form.
findings.quote: Let S be a minimal zero sum sequence of cardinal I(C_n) −1. Then index(S) = 2 if and only if n is odd.
findings.source: Zbl 1205.11029, reviewer L. Gallardo
findings.date_version: zbMATH Open record as read in this screen
findings.scope: Literally false as worded: it drops 'unsplittable', and splittable sequences of this length have index 1. It agrees with Peng–Sun's 'true when n is odd, and false when n is even'.

findings.claim: Yuan, a co-author of the primary result, confirms that Xia–Yuan classify all unsplittable sequences of length ⌊n/2⌋+1.
findings.quote: Remark: Xia and Yuan 2010 (Discrete Math) determined all unsplittable minimal zero-sum sequence of length |S| = ⌊n/2⌋ + 1.
findings.source: P. Yuan, 'Unsplittable minimal zero-sum subsequences over C_n', CANT 2016 Graz, slide 25
findings.verified: read; floor glyphs restored from context

findings.claim: Savchev–Chen: for n≥10, minimal zero-sum sequences of length in [⌊n/3⌋+3, ⌊n/2⌋+1] have a 1- or 2-element basis. The unsplittable ones are u^a v^q (v−su) with 2v=(s+1)u, ⟨u,v⟩=C_n, a q-parity condition, and 2a+(q−1)(s+1)+2=n.
findings.quote: Each minimal zero-sum sequence over C_n, n ≥ 10, with length in [⌊n/3⌋+3, ⌊n/2⌋+1] has a 1-element or a 2-element basis.
findings.source: F. Chen (joint with S. Savchev), CANT 2016 slides 6 and 14–19 (Prop. 2, Thms 3–4). Published as Savchev–Chen, J. Number Theory 177 (2017) 381–427.
findings.verified: Read. The published theorem wording was not checked.
findings.stance: supports: independent cross-check of the p+1 boundary via my own reduction [INFERENCE]

findings.claim: The published version of the Savchev–Chen 'shorter long' characterization exists.
findings.quote: The article characterizes the minimal zero-sum sequences over the cyclic group C_n with lengths between ⌊n/3⌋+3 and ⌊n/2⌋+1, for n ≥ 10.
findings.source: Zbl 1427.11103 (publisher summary) for Savchev–Chen, JNT 177 (2017) 381–427, DOI 10.1016/j.jnt.2017.01.001
findings.read_scope: zbMATH record; full text not read

findings.claim: Savchev–Chen 2007: zero-sum-free sequences of length >n/2 in Z_n have index <1. This is the source of FB's SC0 and, by removing one term, of the index-one theorem.
findings.quote: for each zero-free sequence (a_i) of length ℓ>n/2 in Z_n there is an integer g coprime to n such that if [ga_i] denotes the least positive integer in the congruence class … then Σ[ga_i]<n.
findings.source: S. Savchev, F. Chen, 'Long zero-free sequences in finite cyclic groups', Discrete Math. 307 (2007) 2671–2679
findings.date_version: arXiv math/0602568, submitted 2006-02-25; later versions not checked
findings.scope: Z_n, length >n/2; at n=2p this needs L≥p+1

findings.claim: Zeng–Yuan 2011: a zero-sum sequence of length ≥2⌊n/2⌋+2 with at most two atoms has a generator g whose coefficients sum to 2n. This gives the conclusion of S1-sharp Steps 4/6/7.
findings.quote: let S ∈ F(G) be a zero-sum sequence of length |S| ≥ 2⌊n/2⌋+2. Suppose that S can be decomposed into a product of at most two minimal zero-sum sequences. Then there exists some g ∈ G such that …
findings.source: X. Zeng, P. Yuan, 'Indexes of long zero-sum sequences over cyclic groups', Eur. J. Combin. 32 (2011) 1213–1221, DOI 10.1016/j.ejc.2011.06.007; summary in Zbl 1262.11008
findings.verified: Abstract read; its continuation reads 'S=(n₁g)⋯(n_{|S|}g), n_i∈[1,n], n₁+⋯+n_{|S|}=2n'. Full text 403.
findings.stance: counter: partial overlap that makes part of the S1-sharp proof routine
findings.scope: all cyclic C_n; the abstract also mentions a k≥3 generalization

findings.claim: General-k form: L(S)=k and |S|≥k⌊n/2⌋+2 imply a generator with norm k. For LS this is vacuous when L(T)=3, since it needs |T|≥3p+2.
findings.quote: S ∈ F(G) a zero-sum sequence with L(S) = k ≥ 2 and |S| [≥] k⌊n/2⌋ + 2. Then there exists some g ∈ G with ord(g) = n such that ||S||_g = k.
findings.source: Yuan CANT 2016 slide 21, attributing the result to Zeng–Yuan 2011 EJC
findings.verified: Read. The '≥' and floor glyphs were lost in extraction; my reading is an inference consistent with the k=2 abstract.

findings.claim: Splitting a term can only raise the index; this is used in the p+1 corollary.
findings.quote: if S is a minimal zero-sum sequence and S′ is obtained from S by splitting some elements of S, then |S| [≤] |S′| and ind(S) [≤] ind(S′).
findings.source: W. Gao, Y. Li, P. Yuan, J. Zhuang, Arch. Math. 105 (2015) 361–370, §1
findings.date_version: author preprint PDF dated May 7, 2015; the published version may differ
findings.verified: read; the ≤ glyphs were lost and are restored from context [INFERENCE]

findings.claim: Smoothness for normalized zero-sum-free integer sequences of length >(n+2)/3 that contain 1, with one explicit exception. Applied to odd U of length p in C_2p, the exception cannot occur [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: Let S be a sequence with positive integer terms of length |S| = t > (n+2)/3, and σ(S) < n. If 1 ∈ S, then Σ(S) is an interval except for the case when S = S₀n_l
findings.source: Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang 2015, Thm 11 (exception: Σ(S₀) is an interval and n_l > σ(S₀)+1)
findings.stance: supports (a tool for the parent's REALIZE at L=p)

findings.claim: The two-sided structure theorem for n-zero-sum-free sequences needs length n+ℓ with ℓ≥n/p_min+p_min−2, which is 3p at n=2p. FB's sequences never reach it.
findings.quote: Let p be the smallest prime dividing n, and S be an n-zero-sum free sequence over Z_n of length |S| = n + ℓ, where ℓ [≥] n/p + p − 2 is an integer. Then, there exists g ∈ Z_n such that g + S = 0^h T S′
findings.source: Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang 2015, Cor. 9 (h, |T|, |S′| bounds partly lost in extraction)

findings.claim: Savchev–Chen 2008: n-zero-sum-free sequences of length about 3n/2 or more split into a positive part and a near-zero negative part, each of index below 1. This is the closest analog of FB's structure, but its length range is never reached by odd sequences in C_2p.
findings.quote: (a) S has no zero-sum sequence of length n and h(S) = v₀(S); (b) S = S₁S₂, where S₁, S₂ ∈ F(G) with ||S₁||_g < 1 and ||g − S₂||_g < 1 for some g ∈ G with ord(g) = n.
findings.source: Savchev–Chen, Discrete Math. 308 (2008) 1–8, as restated on Yuan's slide 18. Gao–Jiang–Li–Qi Lemma 2.4 restates the hypothesis as 'length greater than 3n/2 − 1'.

findings.claim: E_k(C_n), zero-sums of length not divisible by k, is a different invariant from the S1-sharp window property.
findings.quote: We denote by E_k(G) the smallest positive integer l such that every sequence S over G of length |S| ≥ l has a zero-sum subsequence of length not divided by k.
findings.source: W. Gao, X. Jiang, Y. Li, H. Qi; JNT 2026, PII S0022314X26000107
findings.scope: Determines E_3(C_n) for 3∤n, and E_k(C_n)=n+1 for ⌈n/2⌉<k<n

findings.claim: disc_ℓ / forbidden-length results ask for a single excluded length, not a transfer between length windows.
findings.quote: disc_ℓ(G) be the smallest positive integer t such that each sequence S over G of length |S| ≥ t has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of length not equal to ℓ.
findings.source: W. Gao, Y. Li, P. Zhao, J. Zhuang, Colloq. Math. 144 (2016) 31–44

findings.claim: arXiv 0903.3458 is about zero-sums of distinct lengths and short normal sequences, not long-window transfer.
findings.quote: we obtain a characterization of short normal sequences over a finite Abelian p-group, thus answering positively a conjecture of Gao for a variety of such groups.
findings.source: B. Girard, 'On the existence of zero-sum subsequences of distinct lengths'
findings.date_version: v1 2009-03-20; latest v4 2012-05-25 per arXiv listing lead

findings.claim: Short zero-sum subsequences of zero-sum sequences: the result is for non-cyclic groups; for cyclic G the interval [exp+1, η−1] is empty.
findings.quote: There exists at least one integer t∈[exp(G)+1,η(G)−1] such that every zero-sum sequence of length exactly t contains a zero-sum subsequence of length in [1,exp(G)].
findings.source: Y. Fan, W. Gao, G. Wang, Q. Zhong, J. Zhuang

findings.claim: The congruence-condition constants (zero-sums of length ≡0 mod d) are direct existence constants. With d=2 over C_p this is the odd-coset setting, but not the window implication.
findings.quote: let s_{dN}(G) denote the smallest integer ℓ ∈ N_0 such that every sequence S over G of length |S| ≥ ℓ has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence T of length |T| ≡ 0 mod d.
findings.source: A. Geroldinger, D. Grynkiewicz, W. Schmid, 'Zero-sum problems with congruence conditions'

findings.claim: Ordered Olson remains listed as open, with no comments on the page.
findings.quote: The above conjecture asserts that this reordering is not needed. Apart from Olson's result, there appears to be very little known about this problem.
findings.source: M. DeVos, Open Problem Garden #155
findings.date_version: posted 2007-03-10; re-read in this screen, unchanged

findings.claim: The ordered result is known only for p-groups. D_2p, of order 2p, is excluded.
findings.quote: we prove our main result which is the strong version of the Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem for arbitrary finite p-groups, answering in the affirmative a conjecture of Olson in the special case of p-groups.
findings.source: V. Dimitrov, Math. Balkanica 18 (2004) 129–140, Zbl 1079.20037 ('Cited in 6 Documents', unchanged from the prior scout)
findings.kind: publisher or author summary via zbMATH

findings.claim: Trap: Dimitrov's MIT RSI paper proves 'D^({n})(G) ≤ 2n−1 for soluble G' (Cor. 3.3.1), but its sequences are unordered, so it is NOT ordered Olson for soluble groups.
findings.quote: Define F(G) to be the free abelian semigroup over G. We can identify sequences of G with the elements of F(G).
findings.source: V. Dimitrov, 'Zero-sum problems in finite groups', MIT RSI (supervisor P. Pylyavskyy)
findings.verified: Read. Prop. 3.1.1's 'minor' argument reorders products; only Prop. 4.0.1 (group algebra, p-groups) is ordered.

findings.claim: Godara–Joshi–Mazumdar's ordered constant D(G) concerns product-one subsequences of any length, not length |G|. Still at v2, with no OpenAlex citations.
findings.quote: there exist 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 <⋯< i_m ≤ k such that g_{i_1}g_{i_2}⋯g_{i_m}=1
findings.source: N. K. Godara, R. Joshi, E. Mazumdar, 'An algebraic approach towards a conjecture on the Davenport constant'
findings.date_version: v1 2024-07-01; v3 returns HTTP 404, so v2 (2025-11-23 per the prior DataCite record) is latest; OpenAlex W4400341991 cited_by_count 0
findings.scope: p-groups, dicyclic, semidihedral and other groups; any-length ordered products

findings.claim: The latest dihedral and metacyclic E(G) work is explicitly unordered and cannot imply the ordered criteria.
findings.quote: A finite collection of elements from G, where the order is disregarded and repetitions are allowed, is said to be a product-one sequence if its elements can be ordered such that their product in G equals the identity
findings.source: J. S. Oh, S. Ribas, K. Zhao, Q. Zhong, 'On zero-sum problems over metacyclic groups C_n ⋊_s C_2'
findings.scope: E(G) and its inverse problem for all C_n⋊_sC_2, unordered

theorem_comparison.lane_statement: p≥5 prime, 0≤κ≤⌊2p/3⌋: an odd Y⊂C_2p with no zero-sum of length in [2κ+2,2p] has no zero-sum of length >2κ. Fails for every κ∈[⌊2p/3⌋+1,p] (F1 = g^{p+3}(3g)^{p−1}).
theorem_comparison.reformulation_INFERENCE: Equivalently, every all-odd zero-sum T with |T|≥2p+2 has a zero-sum subsequence of length in [2⌊2p/3⌋+2,2p]. Via (1,x)↦x, it is a statement about even-length zero-sums over C_p. Under (ZP_κ) with κ≤p−1, EGZ applied twice in C_p forces |Y|≤3p−2.
theorem_comparison.closest_primary: Zeng–Yuan 2011 (k=2); Savchev–Chen 2007 / Yuan 2007 (imports); Gao–Jiang–Li–Qi 2026 (E_k); Gao–Li–Zhao–Zhuang 2016 (disc_ℓ); Geroldinger–Grynkiewicz–Schmid (s_{dN}); Fan et al. 2011
theorem_comparison.relation: Neither the statement nor an equivalent was located. Partial overlap with Zeng–Yuan 2011 [INFERENCE]: once Steps 1–3 make every proper zero-sum of T minimal (at most two atoms, |T|≥2p+2), Zeng–Yuan gives a generator g with coefficient sum 4p, so both atoms Q and Q′ have coefficient sum 2p. That is Step 4's basis plus Steps 6–7, without needing |Q|≥p+3. Not found: Step 5 (the exchange inequality MC), Steps 8–9 (the b_min obstruction and the base≥3 count), and the sharp ⌊2p/3⌋ threshold. The other invariants are existence questions about a single length or residue class, not implications between length windows.
theorem_comparison.bounded_status: NONE-FOUND-IN-SCOPE for the statement; PARTIAL-OVERLAP for the proof route

theorem_comparison.lane_statement: In (S′): take any longest zero-sum Z=g^{n+}N whose zero-sum-free complement has length L≥p+1, normalized by any index-<1 generator g. Then S(N)≤2p−1−W, hence S(N)=n+ and W+n+≤2p−1. No L-versus-2t hypothesis is needed.
theorem_comparison.closest_primary: Savchev–Chen 2007 (the SC0 import); Savchev–Chen 2008 (two-sided n-zero-free structure); Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang 2015 Cor. 9
theorem_comparison.relation: Analogy only. The two-sided theorems need n-zero-sum-freeness at lengths >3n/2−1 (≥3p), or n+ℓ with ℓ≥n/p+p−2 (=3p). FB's sequences have R=2p+2κ−k≤3p−3, and odd sequences without 2p-zero-sums have length ≤3p−2, so both ranges are vacuous here [INFERENCE]. No balance or room lemma for longest zero-sums was located.

theorem_comparison.item: Restricted ordered D_2p criteria (S1-sharp corollary; Corollary INV*/OLSON-FB)
theorem_comparison.lane_statement: (i) For p≥5: every length-(4p−1) word with 3o_F≤2p+1 has an identity 2p-subword in increasing index order. (ii) For p≥7: the same holds when o_F≤p−1 and F−o_F≥2(p−1−⌊2p/3⌋).
theorem_comparison.closest_primary: Ordered: EGZ (abelian); Dimitrov 2004 (p-groups); Olson–White ordered Davenport (any length; as quoted by the prior scout, not re-read); Godara–Joshi–Mazumdar 2407.01148 (any-length ordered Davenport) and their conjecture (prior scout). Unordered: Olson 1976, Bass 2007, Gao–Lu 2008, Oh–Zhong 2020, Oh–Ribas–Zhao–Zhong 2511.18246. Lower bound z(D_2m)≥4m−1 (prior scout).
theorem_comparison.relation: None implies either criterion. The unordered E(D_2n)=3n results allow reordering, and D_2p is not a p-group. Trivial ordered baseline [INFERENCE]: if F≤p (at least 3p−1 rotation letters), two applications of EGZ in the abelian rotation subgroup C_p give 2p rotations with product 1 in any order. The lane criteria allow far larger F.
theorem_comparison.bounded_status: NONE-FOUND-IN-SCOPE; consistent with olson-par-priority-scout-v1 and MondayMathPriority-report-v1, re-checked here (Open Problem Garden page, 2407.01148 version, Dimitrov citation count)

theorem_comparison.item: PARENT QUERY: all-odd minimal zero-sum sequences over C_2p of length p+1 have index 1
theorem_comparison.statement: For p≥5 prime, every all-odd minimal zero-sum sequence over C_2p of length p+1 has index 1. Equivalently, via U·(−σ(U)), every odd zero-sum-free U of length p has index <1.
theorem_comparison.matched_primary: Xia–Yuan 2010 Thm 3.1 (via Peng–Sun's restatement); the splitting monotonicity (Peng–Sun; Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang 2015); I(C_n)=⌊n/2⌋+2 for n≥8 (Savchev–Chen 2007; Yuan 2007).
theorem_comparison.derivation_INFERENCE: (1) For n=2p, both even-n unsplittable forms contain an even term: 2g, or (p+1)g with g of order 2p. So an all-odd S of length p+1 is splittable. (2) Splitting gives a minimal zero-sum S′ of length p+2=I(C_2p), so ind(S′)=1. (3) ‖S‖_g≤‖S′‖_g, so ind(S)=1. (4) For zero-sum-free U of length p, U·(−σ(U)) is minimal and all-odd (p odd terms have odd sum), so ‖U‖_g≤1−1/(2p). Cross-check: the Savchev–Chen unsplittable forms at n=2p and length p+1 force s=1 (v=u+p, so u and u+p both occur) or q=1 (u lies in 2C_2p). Either way there is an even term.
theorem_comparison.sharpness_INFERENCE_hand_checked: General sequences: the parent's g^{p−2}(pg)((p+1)g)^2 is Xia–Yuan's second family with t=p−2, ℓ=1 and has index 2. Odd-only, one step below: g^{p−4}((p+2)g)^2(pg) is minimal and all-odd, of length p−1, with index 2 for every prime p≥7 (e.g. 1^7·13^2·11 over C_22, checked against all units) and index 1 for p=5. Length p cannot occur, since all-odd zero-sums have even length. So among all-odd sequences, index 1 holds at every length ≥p+1 and first fails at p−1.
theorem_comparison.normalization_note_INFERENCE: For normalized U (Σa_i≤2p−1, length p), 1∈U, and the Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang Thm 11 exception S₀n_l would need n_l≥p+1, hence Σa_i≥2p. So Σ(U)=[1,W], and g^{p−1}(pg) is not a smoothness exception. Whether the lane's REALIZE needs more than smoothness was not checked.
theorem_comparison.bounded_status: KNOWN-COROLLARY. Conditional on the accuracy of Peng–Sun's restatement; the Xia–Yuan full text was not read (403).

theorem_comparison.item: LS (unproved length-sensitive conjecture): strongest applicable lemmas, ranked; not asserted
lemmas: EGZ twice in C_p [elementary]: (ZP_κ) with κ≤p−1 forces |Y|≤3p−2, so LS lives in p+2κ+1≤|Y|≤3p−2. At κ=p−2 this means |Y|∈{3p−3,3p−2}.
Zeng–Yuan 2011 (k=2): applies whenever a shortest long zero-sum T has only minimal proper zero-sums (|T|≥2p+2 is automatic). The k≥3 version needs |T|≥3p+2 and is vacuous.
Savchev–Chen 2007: complements of length ≥p+1 have index <1.

Known corollary, new to the lane (row above): odd complements of length exactly p have index <1, and all-odd atoms of length ≥p+1 have index 1. Atoms of length ≤p−1 can have index 2 (the family g^{p−4}((p+2)g)^2(pg)).

Savchev–Chen JNT 2017: 1- or 2-element bases for atoms of length in [⌊2p/3⌋+3,p+1]. [INFERENCE] By the unsplittable forms, no all-odd unsplittable sequence exists in this range, but splitting can introduce even terms.
Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang Thm 11: smoothness of normalized zero-sum-free sequences of length >(2p+2)/3.
Bovey–Erdős–Niven 1975: a zero-sum-free sequence of length ℓ>n/2 has an element of multiplicity ≥2ℓ−n+1 (as quoted by Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang).
Not applicable: Peng–Sun 2014 (prime order only); Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang Thms 3–4 and Zeng–Yuan–Li Acta Arith. 2016 (odd n only); Yuan–Li IJNT 2016 (least prime divisor of n above a bound).
theorem_comparison.bounded_status: No source states or refutes LS; F1/F2 lie below its length threshold (lane LS-scope).

significance.S1-sharp: Modest extension, conditional: no equivalent was located, but part of the proof follows from Zeng–Yuan 2011. Positively, it is a sharp specialist lemma on length windows for odd-coset zero-sums.
significance.FB: Modest extension: a technical exchange lemma; no equivalent located.
significance.restricted_ordered_D2p_corollaries: Modest extension: partial ordered-Olson results for D_2p, where no ordered result was located. A full ordered Olson theorem for D_2p would be potentially substantive specialist work; major is not established.
significance.odd_only_p_plus_1_boundary: Already known / corollary: a two-line consequence of Xia–Yuan 2010 Thm 3.1. Reuse it instead of re-deriving it.

counterpoints: With Zeng–Yuan 2011 and Savchev–Chen 2007 in hand, a specialist may judge S1-sharp routine exchange counting.
Savchev–Chen JNT 2017 (47 pp.) and Zeng–Yuan 2011 were not read in full; their internal lemmas on small terms, standard decompositions or k≥3 structure might contain window-type statements.
Index-theory literature on odd moduli (Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang; Zeng–Yuan–Li) is extensive. Chinese-language papers and theses (Zeng, Xia, Zhuang) were not screened.
The p+1 answer rests on a secondary verbatim restatement and author slides; the only located review (zbMATH) is garbled.
Ordered-status evidence is cumulative bounded screening; unannounced or very recent work cannot be excluded.
open_questions: Do all-odd index-2 atoms occur at every even length in [⌊2p/3⌋+3,p−1]? The 2-element-basis family suggests yes; one explicit family exists at length p−1 for p≥7 [INFERENCE].
Is there a published odd-coset analog of Zeng–Yuan (two atoms or L(T)=3) at lengths ≤3p−2 in C_2p?
